sources.entry: Jotty - Lightweight but powerful alternative for managing your personal, file based, notes and checklists. (Source Code) AGPL-3.0 Docker

summary.one_liner: Jotty (jotty·page) is a self-hosted, lightweight app for personal checklists and notes that stores everything as plain files instead of a database.
summary.what_it_does: Provides checklists with drag-and-drop reordering, progress bars, categories, and task projects with Kanban boards and time tracking. Offers a WYSIWYG rich text notes editor built on TipTap with GitHub Flavored Markdown support and syntax highlighting. Notes and checklists are saved as .md files and users/sessions/sharing data as JSON in a single data directory, so no database is needed. Items can be shared with other users on the instance or through public shareable links. Notes can be encrypted with PGP, and a REST API provides programmatic access. It also includes an admin panel for user management, 14 built-in themes with custom theme support, OIDC single sign-on, MFA, and PWA installation with partial offline caching.
use_cases: Keeping private notes on your own server
Managing task lists with Kanban boards
Sharing checklists with other users or via public links
Automating task creation through a REST API
Running a notes app with single sign-on
how_to_run: Create a docker-compose.yml using image ghcr.io/fccview/jotty:latest, mapping port 1122:3000 and volumes ./data, ./config, and ./cache to /app/data, /app/config, and /app/.next/cache
mkdir -p config data/users data/checklists data/notes data/sharing data/encryption cache
Open the app in a browser and create the admin account at /auth/setup (first user becomes admin)
notable: File-based storage: Markdown and JSON files, no database required
PGP encryption for notes and checklists
Kanban boards and time tracking inside task projects
Supports any OIDC provider for single sign-on
Versioning scheme of STABLE.FEATURE.FIX with automatic migrations
caveats: Running without Docker requires Node.js 24 or later
No offline create/update/delete support; the PWA only lets you revisit pages you already loaded online
Docs for many features (API, encryption, SSO, MFA) are in separate howto files not included in this README
